column8: seat12 2026-09-04 round 5. All 5 forms witnessed, oracle-cut against Rakudo 2026.05 (first draft had CATCH as a sibling block after try{} instead of nested inside it -- caught by the oracle itself, silently produced empty output rather than "caught"; fixed before minting). 1/5 PASS (exceptions_no_catch -- bare `try` with no CATCH swallows and continues, already worked). 4/5 FAIL across THREE distinct parser-level root causes (ablated before filing, confirmed each is independent via minimal isolated repros): (1) `CATCH { }` phaser nested inside `try { }` is not parsed at all -- bare `try { die "x"; }` alone parses fine (ab1), adding a CATCH block breaks it (task raku-catch-phaser-not-parsed; hits exceptions, exceptions_die_message, and downstream of cause 3 on exceptions_specific_type too). (2) the `fail` keyword/builtin is not parsed at all, standalone (`fail "oops";` alone fails -- task raku-fail-keyword-not-implemented; hits exceptions_fail). (3) a `::`-package-qualified name used in EXPRESSION/reference position (`X::AdHoc.new(...)`) does not parse, even with zero args (`X::AdHoc.new()` alone fails) -- but the identical `::`-qualified form in DECLARATION position (`class Foo::Bar { }`) parses fine, and an ordinary unqualified class's `.new(payload => "typed")` named-arg call also parses fine (isolated via ab3/ab4/ab5/ab6, ruling out named-args and declaration-position as the cause) -- task raku-package-qualified-name-not-parsed-in-expression-position; hits exceptions_specific_type (fails on line 2, before ever reaching its own CATCH on a later line, so this witness sits behind cause 3, not cause 1, though fixing 3 alone would likely still hit 1 next). Both modes affected identically (parse-level, mode-3 and mode-4 fail the same way)

column1: rung13
column8: seat12 2026-09-04 round 6. All 5 forms witnessed, oracle-cut against Rakudo 2026.05 (basic method dispatch, single inheritance with 'is' + self-dispatch to the overriding method, named-arg constructor over public has attributes, private \$! attribute encapsulation, public \$. attribute with 'is rw' + external assignment). 4/5 PASS (classes, classes_inheritance, classes_named_arg_constructor, classes_public_attribute). classes_private_attribute FAILs: 'method init { \$!count = 0 }' is a parse error. Ablated to a clean, distinct root cause (11 minimal repros, see task LEDGER): a twigil-sigiled attribute (\$!name or \$.name) parses fine as a bare RVALUE inside a method but never as an LVALUE -- target of '=', ':=', or '++' -- independent of private vs public twigil; external accessor-call writes from OUTSIDE the class ('\$obj.attr = value', see classes_public_attribute, which PASSES) are a different code path and unaffected. Filed raku-twigil-attribute-not-parsed-as-assignment-target with a verified DONE-WHEN. NOTE: this round also found (and reverted before committing) that running scripts/util_build_master_suite.py's default absorb -- even scoped via --absorb-only to just these 5 new families -- resorts/reindexes the ENTIRE existing 907-row raku master as a side effect (rank churn on 906/907 rows, plus silently reintroducing the known say/print/etc. bareword-undercount on ~48 rows that prior rounds had hand-corrected); every prior round's actual committed diff was a clean append-only (e.g. round 5 = +5 lines to ALL.csv, verified via `git show`), so this round hand-appended the same narrow way instead and left the tool's resort behavior uninvestigated -- out of this row's scope, flagged for whoever owns that instrument.

column1: rung14
column8: seat12 2026-09-04, round 7. All 5 forms witnessed, oracle-cut against Rakudo 2026.05 (basic role application via 'does' + a role method, a role attribute combining 'is rw' with a default-value initializer, multi-role composition via 'does A does B', class-method-overrides-role-method precedence, '~~' smartmatch against a role). 3/5 PASS (roles, roles_composition, roles_override). roles_attributes FAILs: 'has $.count is rw = 0;' is a parse error -- ablated to a cause independent of roles (4 minimal repros, see task LEDGER): combining the 'is rw' trait with a default-value initializer on one attribute declaration fails to parse identically inside a plain 'class' body, not just a 'role' body; 'is rw' alone and a default value alone each parse fine separately, only the combination breaks. Filed raku-has-attribute-rw-with-default-value-not-parsed. roles_smartmatch FAILs: '$b ~~ Flyer' is a parse error -- ablated to a cause independent of roles: '~~' against ANY class/role/builtin-type identifier is entirely unparsed (reproduces identically against a plain class and against a builtin type like Int); distinct from '~~' against a regex literal, which DOES parse and run in SCRIP today but returns the wrong value (prints "1" where real Raku prints a stringified Match object, e.g. "｢b｣" -- a separate, not-yet-filed wrong-output bug, flagged here for whoever owns that area, not chased further). Filed raku-smartmatch-against-type-identifier-not-parsed. NOTE: also seen in ablation (not one of this rung's 5 forms, not separately filed): a bare 'say' on an uninitialized/Any-typed attribute prints an empty line where real Raku prints "(Any)" -- similar in flavor to the already-filed raku-undefined-value-raku-method-prints-empty-not-any (which is specifically about '.raku', not bare 'say'); may or may not share a cause, unverified. NOTE: util_build_master_suite.py's RAKU_COLS feature-coverage schema has no 'role'/'does' column at all, so every witness this rung mints is invisible on that census axis -- flagged for whoever owns that instrument, out of a walker's lane to fix.
